name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (architect → explore → design) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → optional /spec:design (mock-bound, deterministic fidelity gates) → /spec:build (direct Sonnet worker dispatch per layer wave, executed red-check) → /spec:review (deterministic legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros; verdict derived by verdict.js) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.10.0 — admission bar hardened to derivation over attestation (same-day amendment of 7.9.0, backed by a May-2026+ research sweep): the five tests are now five separately answered fields, derived from ledger evidence wherever a ledger can answer them — generality names ≥2 ledger-recorded class members (≥1 not the triggering incident), materiality is the cited fleet recurrence count, removability is a kill condition a ledger query answers with a count, falsifiability cites its executed red run — with portability deliberately left as prose because a synthetic second-stack run is fixture evidence and fixture-fed proof is not terminal; a proposal that cannot fill all five fields is a rejection whose reopen condition must itself be ledger-answerable. Rationale: holistic one-line self-certification is the most inflatable shape (halo effect, up to ~50% inflation in cited studies) while computed numbers cannot be talked into existence. Roadmap brief 17 (fleet evidence reader) is named the bar's evidence source and gains its invocation point — it runs whenever a guard is proposed or a rejection's reopen condition is evaluated — and its escape-aggregate query now flags recurrent-unguarded classes (≥3 recurrences, no standing guard), pricing the bar's rejection bias. Doctrine + roadmap prose only — no script, no schema, no host contract change. 7.9.0 — admission bar for standing guards: core.md § Incident Policy now requires that a guard earned by third recurrence also pass five admission tests — portable across host stacks, general to the class rather than the triggering instance, material (value exceeds maintenance + reading cost), falsified once (deliberately tripped to prove it can go red), and shipped with the kill condition that would retire it — and a proposal that cannot state all five in one line becomes a rejection with a reopen condition; this writes down the missing half of the policy (it said when a guard is earned, never what shape an admitted guard must have), generalizing the v6 post-mortem where findings became per-case pins shaped like their triggering incidents, none falsified and none removable. Doctrine prose only — no script, no schema, no host contract change. 7.8.1 — entry-point conformance: a new central manifest `spec/entrypoints.json` declares, per executable in `spec/scripts/*.js|*.sh` (excluding `spec/scripts/lib/`) and `spec/workflows/*.js`, which files invoke it, and `tests/consistency/entrypoints.test.js` diffs those declarations against the live repo in four directions on every `npm test` — inventory forward (a script with no entry, or an empty `entryPoints`, is red: there is no sanctioned orphan form), inventory reverse (a manifest key naming a missing file is red), invocation forward (a declared entry point that no longer carries the invocation literal is red), and invocation reverse (a `spec-paths <key>` or hooks.json call site the manifest does not declare is red); this closes the third recurrence of the authored-but-never-activated class (env-preflight absent from review was the third instance, closed in 7.7.0) with a deterministic guard per core § Incident Policy, its checker logic living in the test file as pure functions over an injectable root, exercised against the live repo as a green pin and against tmpdir fixtures for each red case so no red path is unfalsifiable. The guard's first catch, on the day it landed: `spec/scripts/advisory-append.js` is DELETED along with its `spec-paths advisory-append` key, its usage-line token, and `tests/advisory-append/` — its sole producer was the `wf-review` workflow's `smells` return, which v7 removed, leaving the script with no caller since (adjudicated by the user at build time). The reverse check considers only `spec-paths` keys resolving inside the executable inventory — nine live keys (`shared`, `shared-design`, `shared-genesis`, `replay-corpus`, `template`, `feedback-template`, `templates`, `contract`, `workflows`) resolve to doctrine files, templates, or directories and are not script invocations, so the domain is a glob-shape test rather than an on-disk listing and a stale case-table key pointing at a deleted script still surfaces instead of being silently swallowed. Deliberately out of scope: no `observed`-grammar declarations in the manifest (spec 03's executed pair test owns grammar liveness by execution), and no dynamic-invocation detection — an entry flagged `"dynamic": true` keeps only the file-existence check, and no entry needed that flag at seeding. The manifest is data about the plugin: no host contract change, no grounding-contract edit, no config key. Landing alongside the entry-point work, D13: `ac-matrix.js`'s `missing-test-file` check asserted existence for every `tests`-layer File Plan row regardless of the row's Action, so a spec that PLANS a test file's deletion produced a HARD finding by construction — surfaced by this spec's own D7 deletion row, the repo's first `tests`-layer DELETE. The check now exempts rows whose Action is `DELETE` and stays fail-closed everywhere else: an explicit `CREATE` naming a missing file still raises, and a row in a File Plan table that binds no Action column at all still raises. Pinned by a three-arm behavioral test so "fixed" cannot silently mean "disabled".
